differential: Nephrolithiasis (kidney stone)
Acute onset of severe unilateral flank pain is the classic presentation of renal colic from an obstructing ureteral stone.
Pyelonephritis
Acute bacterial infection of the kidney can present with unilateral flank pain, though typically accompanied by fever and dysuria.
Renal infarction
Acute arterial occlusion to the kidney causes sudden severe flank pain, though less common than nephrolithiasis.
Acute appendicitis (retrocecal)
A retrocecal appendix can cause right flank pain, though typically also presents with peritoneal signs and migration from periumbilical region.
Musculoskeletal strain
Acute flank pain can result from muscle or ligamentous injury, though severity and acute onset make this less likely.
